hypothesis: If display contests are wars of attrition in which each contestant draws a persistence time from an exponential distribution, then the durations of contests that end without escalation (the shorter of two independent exponential draws, which is itself exponential) should follow an exponential distribution.
pass_criterion: Pre-registered. Data: 'Vibrating aggression: spider males perform an unusual assessment strategy during contest displays', Dryad doi:10.5061/dryad.bg79cnpjg, file fight.csv (male-male contests of the orb-web spider Trichonephila clavipes), restricted to contests recorded as not escalating to physical contact, using the contest duration column as given. SUPPORTS if n >= 20 AND a Kolmogorov-Smirnov test of exponentiality with the rate estimated from the data (p-value calibrated by 10,000 parametric bootstrap replicates, i.e. a Lilliefors-type test) gives p > 0.05 AND the coefficient of variation of the durations lies in [0.7, 1.3].
fail_criterion: Pre-registered. REFUTES if the bootstrap-calibrated test gives p < 0.01 AND the coefficient of variation lies outside [0.5, 1.5]. MIXED otherwise. INCONCLUSIVE (underpowered) if n < 20. INCONCLUSIVE (data-unavailable) if Dryad keeps blocking automated download (as of 2026-10-31 it serves a JavaScript proof-of-work challenge to scripted requests, which this project does not circumvent) and no manually downloaded copy with a recorded checksum is supplied.
interpretation: The ESS of the symmetric war of attrition with cost linear in time is an exponential persistence time with mean equal to the resource value V; observed contest duration is the minimum of two such draws and so is exponential with mean V/2. Resource value is not varied in this dataset, so only the distributional prediction is tested, not the scaling of the mean with V. Durations are presumably recorded from the start of display with some time resolution, which can produce a floor; this is examined as a caveat if the data are obtained.
